what_happened: The the person running Athena wrote a "keep a batch running" request that asked for two changes in one job. The first was to skip a failing item so the batch continues. The second was to sort repeated failures by shared cause. The plan grew from 15 to 22 steps. The writer ran out of time. The batch stopped again on the same bug. The the person running Athena replaced the request with one that makes a single change. This was an intervention note, not a failed job record.
cause: Athena has no size check on a request or plan before dispatch, and no rule that urgent unblocking fixes go alone. A request with two separable outcomes is accepted as one job. Nothing flags the second outcome as independent of the first. The plan's growth (15 to 22 steps) is not compared with what one writer run can finish. The failure shows only when the deadline passes, and the bug that stops the batch stays unfixed meanwhile. The existing classes cover the reading taking in too much and the critic not holding plans to a size bound. Neither covers an the person running Athena-written request that bundles an urgent fix with extra work.
prevention: Add a check at request admission and again at plan acceptance. At admission, flag a request that states more than one independent outcome, such as "and also" or two separate verbs of change. Hold it, or ask for a split, when one of the outcomes unblocks a stopped drain. At plan acceptance, compare the step count against a cap and against the producer's deadline. A plan above the cap goes back to be split into a first job that lands the unblocking fix and a follow-up job for the rest. Until the check exists, the default is that a request to unblock a stopped queue holds exactly one change, and any reclassification or reporting work is queued separately behind it.
proposed_request: Add a size and bundling check to the plan stage. When a plan for a job exceeds a step cap (start with 16 steps, set in athena.toml), or when the accepted reading lists more than one independent outcome and one of them is a fix for a stopped drain, the plan is not sent to the producer. Athena instead records a split: a first job with only the unblocking fix, and a follow-up job with the other outcomes, queued behind it. Acceptance: (1) a plan of 22 steps is split and the first job holds only the skip-failing-item change; (2) a plan of 15 steps with one outcome goes through unchanged; (3) the split is shown in the job record with the reason; (4) a test replays the two requests from this case, the bundled one and the one-change replacement, and checks that the first is split and the second is not.
